[h1] Get this and then get OpenRCT2 [/h1]

Roller Coaster Tycoon 1 & 2 are among the greatest games of all time. They are still just as fun today as they were when I played them as a kid, and you will not regret buying them today. That being said, they [i]can[/i] be improved. RCT 2 has lackluster scenarios compared to the first game. The expansions, unfortunately, are pretty terrible.

The worst thing however, is that by buying this game, you are giving money to Atari, the impostor killers of the franchise. They dragged the RCT name through the mud and now the brand is relegated to horrible mobile games and the like. They at the very least let you still buy the actually good games - but it is like having to pay the man who murdered your grandfather for permission to visit your grandfather's old house.


OpenRCT2 is an open source fan project that fixes many of the problems of RCT, and [i]will[/i] fix that last one. If you have RCT2 installed, you get a vastly improved version of the original game. You get bugfixes, quality of life modern amenities, the ability to download scenarios from RCT 1 and custom scenarios. You get literal decades of fan custom scenery. You get multiplayer. You get improvements to scenario play.

What I've found the most fun with is the cheats unlocking immense potential in creative play, allowing you to make amazing fantasy and realistic builds in the game. There is a thriving OpenRCT2 creative community out there, with stuff like Deurklink Multiplayer and Head 2 Head on new element.

OpenRCT2  unlocks all of this and more, like several new official coasters like the hybrid and single rail, as well as new music. It's not too difficult to install either. There is no reason to play the original when you can play it significantly improved with OpenRCT2.

The cherry on top - it's still a good few years out, it's hard too gauge timelines on fan projects - but the ultimate goal of OpenRCT2 is, like OpenTTD, to eventually replace all the original game's assets with similar versions, enabling OpenRCT2 to be released for free, finally breaking from Atari's shackles.

So by all means, get RCT2, and then download OpenRCT2. You will not regret it.

A Thrilling Ride Through RollerCoaster Tycoon® 2: Triple Thrill Pack

Rating: ★★★★☆

RollerCoaster Tycoon® 2: Triple Thrill Pack takes players on a wild and exhilarating journey into the world of amusement park management. Building upon the success of its predecessor, this classic simulation game offers an abundance of content, creative freedom, and addictive gameplay that will keep fans entertained for hours on end.

One of the standout features of Triple Thrill Pack is the sheer variety of options available to players. From designing and constructing custom roller coasters to managing the park's finances and attending to the needs of visitors, there is no shortage of tasks to tackle. The inclusion of three expansion packs—Wacky Worlds, Time Twister, and the original RollerCoaster Tycoon® 2—adds an incredible amount of additional content, giving players even more options for expanding their park and testing their management skills.

The game's interface is intuitive and easy to navigate, making it accessible to both newcomers and seasoned players. Constructing rides, paths, and scenery is a breeze, thanks to the simple yet powerful tools at your disposal. The attention to detail in the park management aspect is impressive, allowing players to fine-tune every aspect of their park's operation, from ticket prices to staff management. The ability to customize everything, including the appearance of your rides and the landscape, adds a layer of personalization that enhances the overall experience.

Triple Thrill Pack's graphics, while not cutting-edge by today's standards, still hold up well and retain their charm. The colorful and vibrant visuals capture the essence of a lively amusement park, and the animations bring the rides and attractions to life. The sound design complements the gameplay, with upbeat music and a range of sound effects that immerse players in the park atmosphere.

The game's longevity is unquestionable. With a multitude of scenarios to conquer, sandbox mode for unlimited creativity, and the ability to download and share user-created content, there is always something new to discover. The inclusion of the expansion packs ensures that players can continue to expand and diversify their park, prolonging the game's replayability and enjoyment.

However, it is worth noting that Triple Thrill Pack's AI and pathfinding mechanics can be occasionally frustrating. Park visitors sometimes exhibit strange behavior or encounter difficulties navigating the park's pathways, leading to minor inconveniences. While these issues are not game-breaking, they can detract from the overall experience.

In conclusion, RollerCoaster Tycoon® 2: Triple Thrill Pack is a superb amusement park management simulation that has stood the test of time. Its wealth of content, creative freedom, and addictive gameplay make it a must-play for fans of the genre. Despite some minor AI quirks, the game's immersive experience, combined with the ability to unleash your imagination, guarantees an enjoyable and thrilling ride for both new players and nostalgic fans alike.

RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 is not just a game—it’s a timeless masterpiece that defined what theme park management sims could be. It’s the kind of game you can play for hours and still feel like you’ve barely scratched the surface.

What I Love About It:
Endless Creativity
The game’s sandbox-style gameplay allows you to create parks limited only by your imagination. Want to build a massive, sprawling theme park with intricate coaster designs? Go for it. The customization options are incredible, from terrain editing to coaster building.

The Nostalgic Graphics
The pixelated, isometric visuals are iconic. They might not be modern, but they’re packed with charm and clarity. The style is clean, functional, and still a joy to look at, even years later.

Scenario-Based Gameplay
Unlike later entries, the focus on pre-made scenarios gives the game a structured challenge. Each park comes with unique goals that test your skills, keeping the gameplay engaging and rewarding.

Chris Sawyer’s Genius
The game was created by a single developer, and you can feel the love and care poured into every detail. It’s a pure passion project that stands out even in today’s gaming landscape.

The Community Mods and Custom Scenarios
Even years after its release, the game has a thriving fanbase that keeps it alive with custom content. From new scenarios to innovative coaster designs, there’s always something fresh to try.

Why It’s a Timeless Classic:
RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 is a perfect blend of creativity, challenge, and charm. It doesn’t try to overcomplicate things—it focuses on giving players the tools to build their dream parks while offering satisfying objectives.

Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)
Whether you’re a long-time fan or discovering it for the first time, RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 remains one of the best theme park simulation games of all time. It’s a game that never loses its magic.

If you're wondering why Steam says I have less than an hour of play time with this game, it's because I got this and RollerCoaster Tycoon 1 Deluxe for OpenRCT2, which I've sunk more time into.

And now for a quick history lesson on this game: Its original American release date was in late 2002. Its first expansion pack (note that I didn't say DLC, because it had a physical release), Wacky Worlds, was released in 2003. Later that year, its second expansion pack, Time Twister, came out. Both add new scenarios, scenery with various themes, and reskins of rides that were already in the base game.

Around the same time that Time Twister released, the Combo Park Pack (as it's known in America, which is where I life), a compilation of the base RCT2 game and Wacky Worlds, came out. The following year, the Triple Thrill Pack, a compilation of the base RCT2 game and both of its expansion packs, released. This Steam release is a digital version of the Triple Thrill Pack.

Anyway, onto my pros and cons list!

PROS:
Messing with your customers, such as by raising the price of umbrellas when it starts raining or selling free (salty) French fries and overpriced drinks next door, is a lot of fun
Killing your guests on purpose is a lot of fun, though even one death at your park causes its rating to plummet (and if that death was from a ride crashing, guests will avoid it for months even if no one dies)
Playing the game how you're supposed to can also be fun

CONS:
Many of your guests are cowards
(I'd have other complaints, but that'd just be me being spoiled by what OpenRCT2 adds to the game that neither RCT2 nor RCT1 have officially, like fast forwarding, winning the scenario early if you reach the goal long before the deadline, auto-saving, online multiplayer, and more)

Overall, it's up to you if you want to get this game, though I'd recommend you pick up and play OpenRCT2 if you choose to buy this.

Roller Coaster Tycoon 2 is a game that I sunk many hours into back in the day. Building my own amusement parks, filled with rides and attractions, was a blast. The game's mechanics were intuitive and easy to pick up, but there was still a lot of depth to be found in managing the parks and keeping guests happy.

One thing that really takes RCT2 to the next level is the OpenRCT2 project. This community-driven effort has added all kinds of new features and improvements to the game, from bug fixes and quality-of-life changes to new rides and customization options. It's amazing how much of a difference these tweaks can make in the overall experience.

But even without OpenRCT2, RCT2 is still a fantastic game. There's something really satisfying about watching your park grow and evolve over time, as you add new attractions and tweak existing ones to keep guests coming back for more. And when you finally get that coaster just right, with all the thrills and excitement you could ask for, it's hard not to feel like a genius.

Of course, RCT2 is not without its quirks and frustrations. Sometimes guests will get stuck or lost, or refuse to ride certain attractions for no apparent reason. And when a ride breaks down, it can be a real headache to get it back up and running again. But overall, these issues are just minor bumps in the road of what is otherwise an incredibly fun and engaging game.

In conclusion, if you're looking for a game that will let you live out your wildest amusement park dreams, then Roller Coaster Tycoon 2 is definitely worth checking out. And if you really want to take things to the next level, be sure to install OpenRCT2 and see what the community has cooked up. You won't be disappointed.

Short Review: Rollercoaster Tycoon 2: Triple Thrill Pack is the sequel to a great game that replicates everything that the first one did well and improves it, adding more exciting content and new challenges that will truly bring the park manager inside you to life. This revision of the game adds the base game and the two original expansions for a mere 5 dollars, which honestly feels like a steal, not in a bad way, but rather because this game, just like its prequel, has a lot to offer and a high level of replayability.

Repeating myself from my RT1 review, its 2.5d graphics might be a bit archaic for today's standards but have aged fairly well and can be considered "retro" rather than "dated", specially in comparison to the 3D ones of the third installment. 
There is a lot to do in this game and each park provides its own set of challenges that must be overcome in order to reach the desired goals, but as to how you do it, anything goes really, so you can take your sweet time to do it, even if there's a timer for it, don't stress yourself, cause this game is not meant for that but rather to relax. 

This game adds what i desired the most in the first one, a Scenario Editor that, while archaic and a bit clunky to nagivate at times, it has it own charm and has a lot of functionality and customization to it, which really adds a lot of value over the first one. If you're looking for the nostalgia factor with quality of life features this installement of the franchise is for you.

Go, give it a try, and if you're not convinced grab it on sale. If you, for whatever reason, despise the 2.5d graphics of this game, go grab Rollercoaster Tycoon 3, see how badly it has aged in comparison (speaking of graphics, not gameplay).

The classic isometric pixel art may look dated, but it still holds a unique charm. The cheerful (and sometimes hilariously annoying) guest sounds, along with the catchy background music, make the experience feel just like it did back in the early 2000s.

I got this game for free from a cereal box many years ago, and it was one of the first PC games I ever played, so it was cool to revisit the game again after all these years. There are lots of aspects of this game that do feel quite old, but it's still quite fun.

You're given a set of different scenarios and maps, and asked to build a profitable theme park by placing paths, stalls, decorations, and rides. it's quite entertaining to go from a large empty plot of land to a bustling theme park filled with hundreds of guests. It's a good thing it's so entertaining to watch though, as there tends to be a lot of waiting in this game, as you often run out of money and must wait for the park to make enough money back to build the next large ride. Additionally, although there's a good variety of different maps and scenarios which present different challenges, building a park tends to be pretty similar each time, so the game starts to feel quite repetitive after a while.

The game uses an isometric view, which gives it that iconic look you're probably familiar with, and it works fine most of the time, but it can be annoying to try and see things sometimes, as foliage or rides often get in the way. Things tend to be fairly small as well, which also makes things a bit hard to see. The UI also uses windows for everything, which makes it feel quite old, and can make keeping things organized a bit of a nightmare sometimes. Once you adjust the settings and controls to your liking and get used to everything, it's not too bad though.

If you do end up getting this game, I'd highly recommend checking out [url=openrct2.org/]OpenRCT2[/url], an open-source re-implementation of RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 that adds new features and fixes bugs, and helps the game feel not quite as old.  I didn't run into any bugs while playing game and it ran fairly well, which was likely due to the fixes made by OpenRCT2. You can even launch OpenRCT2 through Steam and let Steam track your playtime if you set the launch options for this game to the OpenRCT2 executable like so:
[code]"C:\...\OpenRCT2\openrct2.exe" %COMMAND%[/code]

[b]TL;DR[/b] This old-school theme park management game still has fun gameplay after all these years, even if it is getting a bit dated at this point. Despite some frustrations with the camera, very old UI design, and some fairly repetitive gameplay, it was still fun to revisit, and OpenRCT2 helps lessen some of the design flaws of the game as well. It's age means that it's probably not for everyone, but if you enjoy these kinds of management games or you enjoy old-school PC games in general, I'd recommend trying this one out.

I've been playing RCT2 since I was 8, and now I'm approaching 30. It's an excellent retro game that is just as good now as it was when I was a child, though I have a much better understanding of the game now. 

I'll try to review it for a modern audience's expectations, since if you're looking for the classic/nostalgia then you probably already know the game quite well. The Triple Thrill pack is worth noting for returning players, you get more themes, scenarios, and items than in the base game.

By modern standard the graphics are not great in terms of realism but they are classic/cute/chibi.

The gameplay is a lot of fun, and the economy of the parks is more balanced than some other games: you can either make profit with rides or entrance fees, whereas some other management sims have wildly unbalanced economies like a zoo game where the best strategy is to sell the guests a bunch of junk rather than focussing on the animals.

I recommend RCT2 if you want a chill classic game, and I recommend RCT3 if you want a bit more realism. Frankly the Planet Coaster series and also Rollercoaster Tycoon World have not lived up to my expectations, I strongly recommend RCT2/RCT3 over them.

My one criticism of the RCT2 game is that a lot of the objectives are like "To have at least X guests in your park by year Y" and you don't get credit for completing the scenario earlier than that, you have to wait until Y. This can lead to a situation where you easily achieve a scenario's objectives long before the deadline so you're just sat waiting for the deadline with nothing in particular to do. It's easy to create your own objectives in such a scenario (repay the loan, accumulate $10,000, put one of every ride in the park" so there's no lack of gameplay if you're willing to make your own challenges.

RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 is one of the all-time classic video-game releases and continues to be fondly remembered by many. It is a game all about creating and managing your own amusement park, and the hours of fun and challenge it offers make it a must-have for any fan of the simulation genre.

Players begin the game by creating their own theme park. Everything from park admission, rides, games, landscaping, staff and shops are all customizable. The game's vivid graphics put players in the heart of the action, allowing them to create and manage their own amusement park just the way they'd like it.

A major attraction of the game is its engagement of players in an economy system. Players need to carefully manage their budget to make a profit and purchase land and attractions to grow their park. Rides are the main attraction and the game boasts numerous customizable designs with plenty of exciting special effects and variety.

In addition, players can build a variety of other attractions into their park, such as restaurants, shops, and more. Working with the game's construction and design tools, they can create exciting and personal touches with the environment and the scenery. Plus, the game's challenge increases as players progress in creating a successful amusement park. By researching for new rides, attractions, and decorations, designing the layout of the park, and keeping the money coming in, they can make their park more impressive and attract more visitors.

Overall, RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 is one of the most popular and enduring simulation games ever made. With its colorful visuals, engaging economy system, and wealth of customisable options, the game offers great replay value, allowing players to come back again and again to experiment with new design ideas, attractions, and scenarios. It's a timeless classic and a must-have for anyone looking for the classic sandbox simulation experience.

[h1]A sequel to one of the best video games of all time, and it's even better now with OpenRCT2.[/h1]

Way back when, 8 year old me got this game in a cereal box, and it single-handedly changed my life. RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 is arguably the most iconic tycoon game ever made besides maybe the first game.

[b]NOTE:[/b] Just like the first game, this game tends to crash quite a bit on modern systems if you don't use OpenRCT2. This doesn't make the game unplayable by any means, but it does mean that you should save your game often, which you should ideally be doing anyway. If you plan on playing with OpenRCT2, you won't have this problem.

RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 is basically the first game, but with [i]more[/i]. Everything about the first game that was great (which is basically everything) carries over to this game as well. This game features a lot of new rides, a refined scenery building system, and new possibilities for coaster building. The first game didn't have a sandbox mode, and this game has got one even though it's not a true "sandbox" mode by its strictest definition. So far, this game sounds like a strict upgrade over the first game which I already thought was an 11/10 game, and that would be true...

... If the scenario design didn't take a back seat. The one true downside of RCT2 compared to the first game is that the scenario design and the difficulty curve of those scenarios is quite a bit weaker compared to the first game. Whereas every park in the first game felt like every single tile of terrain was thoughtfully considered to create the best looking landscape, there are quite a few parks in this game that were obviously made in about 5 minutes with the mountain tool from the Scenario Editor. The difficulty curve also takes massive spikes and drops as some scenarios are placed in the wrong difficulty section. Since you can play all the parks in any order you want with all of them unlocked from the beginning of the game, this isn't really that intrusive, but if you play through the game feeling like something is "off" compared to the first game... this is why.

The environment could be entirely flat for all I care because the park building in this game is just as good as it was in the first game. In fact, it's even better because the game has quite a few quality of life elements added to it, and of course there's also the sandbox mode. RCT1 is the better game for those of you that wish to challenge yourself with the scenarios and build a park around the landscapes you're given. RCT2 is the better game if you just want to let your creative juices flow and build the theme park of your dreams. Ideally, you should get both though. Number 1, because they're both two of the best PC games ever made and you can spend thousands of hours of your time on it for less than $15, and number 2, because having both of them is great for OpenRCT2.

OpenRCT2 is simply a game changer. It allows you to play this game with all of the RCT1 scenarios with RCT2's gameplay features, quality of life changes, additions, and better stability for modern hardware.

"RollerCoaster Tycoon 2" is the second instalment in the beloved RollerCoaster Tycoon series, a theme park simulation game developed by Chris Sawyer Productions and published by Atari. Released in 2002, it builds upon the success of the original game, offering enhanced features and more creative opportunities for players. Here's a review of "RollerCoaster Tycoon 2":

**Title: A Timeless Classic in Theme Park Simulation**

**Rating: ★★★★★**

**Pros:**

1. **Deep Gameplay:** "RollerCoaster Tycoon 2" offers a deep and engaging gameplay experience. Players take on the role of a theme park manager, tasked with building and managing their own amusement park. The game provides numerous tools and features to design, customise, and manage every aspect of your park.

2. **Variety of Rides and Attractions:** The game offers a wide variety of rides, roller coasters, and attractions to choose from. Building and customising these attractions, from gentle rides to intense coasters, allows for endless creativity.

3. **Scenarios and Objectives:** The game presents players with a series of scenarios, each with specific objectives and challenges to complete. These scenarios provide a sense of progression and purpose, encouraging players to expand and improve their parks.

4. **Sandbox Mode:** In addition to the scenarios, "RollerCoaster Tycoon 2" features a sandbox mode that allows players to build and experiment without the constraints of objectives. This mode is perfect for unleashing creativity and crafting your dream amusement park.

5. **Modding Community:** Over the years, the game has developed a strong modding community, which has created custom content, scenarios, and tools that extend the game's lifespan and add even more replay-ability.

**Cons:**

1. **Graphics:** While the game's graphics were decent for its time, they are somewhat dated by today's standards. Modern players may find the visuals less appealing compared to newer simulation games.

2. **Learning Curve:** "RollerCoaster Tycoon 2" has a learning curve, particularly for newcomers to the series or the simulation genre. Understanding the game's mechanics, optimizing ride designs, and managing finances effectively can take some time.

3. **Path Building:** Constructing and modifying paths and walkways can be a bit challenging and less intuitive than desired. This aspect of park design may require patience and practice.

4. **Limited Modern Features:** Compared to newer entries in the genre, "RollerCoaster Tycoon 2" lacks some modern features and conveniences, such as advanced AI behaviours and more sophisticated graphics.

In summary, "RollerCoaster Tycoon 2" is a classic and highly enjoyable theme park simulation game that has aged remarkably well. Its deep gameplay, creative opportunities, and scenario-driven progression provide a fulfilling and engaging experience for fans of simulation games. Despite its age and some minor shortcomings, it remains a timeless title in the genre and is a must-play for anyone who enjoys building and managing their own virtual theme park.

RCT2 is less of a sequel, and more of a 'remaster' or 'expanded edition' of the first game. 

	Everything is essentially the same, minus a few quality of life and game mechanic changes. And I mean 'few'. The most obvious one is being able to hold the Shift key to adjust height on scenery and rides. Previously you could do this, but only via roundabout ways (such as raising land then lowering it). You also can't adjust ride prices or park entrace fees as before—now it's either one or the other (or neither at all). Which is actually a decent change, since you could always somewhat cheat the scenario objectives by altering prices to increase satisfaction ratings or revenue.

	RCT1 scenarios were typically "Have x amount of guests with a satisfaction rating of Y by G amount of years". RCT2 has many such scenarios, but some measure success on metrics that either weren't used in the first game, or sparesly used. "Have 10 coasters with an excitement rating of at least Y", that sort of thing. I assume the developer realized how much coaster building was the main draw, so a few scenarios give you unlimited cash to build as you please. Which is, like the prices change, a very nice improvement.

	The main draw of RCT2 and the reason for its existence is the editor. You can finally create your own maps, and even fill them with custom rides and objectives without worrying about monetary constraints. There's really not much more to say about it, other than it does its job well and was sorely lacking before. You can forego the scenarios and just make custom dream parks.

	Editor aside, both games play exactly the same. You have a list of premade scenarios (with pre-made maps) that task you with some manner of objective; RCT2 having more variety than 1 in this category. RCT2 features more stalls and scenery options, so you can build up your park with more rides and food vendors than before. The main draw, of course, is the roller coaster building. And RCT2 has far more coaster varieties than the first game, with unique ride carts per scenario. 

	Coasters (and editor) aside, does this replace RCT1 in its entirety? Not entirely; RCT1 still has its own unique scenario maps. I find some of the maps in 2 to be cluttered with a lot of scenery or significant changes in elevation. You still have plenty of flat maps that are easy to build in and around, but the cluttered ones do stick out. I also feel as if the first game gave you more variety in park sizes and the shape of the play area, but a person with more hours in both games can confirm or deny that. Ultimately, people will play favorites with what maps they liked in each game.

	If it was 2002, I might wonder if its a letdown that a sequel 3 years in development feels more like an expansion pack. Goes to show you that reviews and scores change depending on when you review and whether you're comparing it to a predecessor. In 2021, I'm ok with an enhanced follow-up. As such, if RCT1 is a 7, this is an 8 for the minor improvements.

I remember getting this game in a cereal box way back in the day and having a blast learning to build roller coasters and drowning guests. This was one of the first games I ever played, and I decided to check it out again as an adult and its still a ton of fun. This game is honestly a marvel for its era. Certantly the deffinitive out of the isometric Rollercoaster Tycoon games, although that list consists of two entries. It's also from the time when sequels would come out only a year or two after the previous entry and just be an improvement on what was rather than something more extensive and possibly destructive. RCT2 can more or less replace RCT1 in all aspects.
I wouldn't be so bold as to proclaim it the best Themepark Tycoon game, nor even the best RCT game overall. That's however not because it's not a good game, far from it. It's more so that there exists three other entries within this small niche that make it hard to crown a champion. The best RCT game stands between 2 and 3, where both have their strenghts and weaknesses inherent in their design. Both are really good and stand on their own. Then there exists Parkitect and Planet Coaster, spiritual successors to RCT2 and RCT3 respectively. I haven't played either enough to say wheter they live up to what they are aping, but I feel that we should be so lucky as to have four very good games vying to be the best title in a very small sub-genre born out of a Scottsman's facination with rollercoasters.
